To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the knowledge needed to understand language and vision includes expectations about what is likely to occur and the ability to recognize and adapt to expectation failures, (b) a frame system is a reasonable approach to representing the background knowledge that is required to understand language, and (c) the knowledge required to understand language and visual scenes is not numerical in nature.

(a) the most important aspect of knowledge representation is not the form, but the content of the knowledge; and that (b) the content of knowledge is best represented as a network of interrelated expectations, which are themselves represented as frames, with the details of the expectations represented as slots.

(1) vision is a process that forms expectations and then uses details to fill in the slots in those expectations; (2) the content of the expectations is determined by the knowledge in the system, which can be represented by frames; (3) frames are the best way to represent knowledge in a system that is designed to understand natural language text.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the representation of knowledge about the world in a form which is suitable for reasoning.
developing a framework for representing knowledge in the form of frames and with developing the content of such a knowledge base in the form of expectations.
the problem of understanding natural language text, and we are developing a theory of how to use knowledge about the world and about language to understand text.
